response.message:
Your saves are loaded up on Tokyo, which is great. your list is thin up front though, so [Kyoto](kebi://area/jp/kyoto) and Osaka are where i'll fill in the gaps. here's the trip stop by stop.

---

Kyoto

nothing saved here yet, so this one's on me. Kyoto is an early-morning city, the big spots fill up fast.

[Fushimi Inari Taisha](kebi://venue/798aea34-b234-4a06-b628-8d791d2396bf) is the one to anchor around. the thousands of torii gates winding up the mountain are the image everyone knows, and you've got the whole trail or just the lower gates depending on energy. go at sunrise and the lower section is nearly empty, it's a genuinely different place before the crowds arrive.

[Kinkaku-ji](kebi://venue/1bb9b7c1-bd65-4d69-acf9-3f023cd24844) pairs well with [Arashiyama Bamboo Forest](kebi://venue/f4b47463-0468-4adb-95a6-71f8a4b65393) in the same western loop. go right when Kinkaku-ji opens, it gets shoulder-to-shoulder by mid-morning, then head west to Arashiyama after.

[Kiyomizu-dera](kebi://venue/f8d8b1da-95bf-49fc-ade3-8433f3424185) is the hillside temple with the big wooden stage jutting out over the valley, the views over the city are worth it, and the lanes leading up through Higashiyama are one of the best walks in Japan. evenings are beautiful here too, especially if they're doing the seasonal illuminations.

for food, [Junsei](kebi://venue/b2fc7256-7495-4882-9f42-9ea9bae445eb) near Nanzenji is a lovely traditional tofu kaiseki spot in an old garden setting, the kind of Kyoto lunch that earns its own afternoon. very TikTok-worthy in the best way, not in a gimmicky way.

---

Kyoto to Osaka

only about 15 minutes on the shinkansen or 30 on the express. Fushimi Inari is on the southern edge of Kyoto, basically pointing toward Osaka, if you do it on your last Kyoto morning, rolling out to Osaka from there is a smooth move.

---

Osaka

[Dotonbori](kebi://venue/1b247b82-0663-4f4f-be22-875f5ccc0a9f) is the anchor and it earns it, the neon canal strip at night is genuinely one of those Japan moments. eat here: takoyaki, okonomiyaki, kushikatsu. evening is when it's best.

[Kuromon Market](kebi://venue/e35b0bea-bc55-4afb-adb5-a9cb8391e1b1) is your daytime food move, a covered market with fresh seafood and street snacks, go in the morning when the stalls are fullest.

[Osaka Castle](kebi://venue/15a9d47a-0fb6-44ec-89ac-e7fb01492588) is a good half-morning, the grounds are beautiful and the museum inside covers the history well.

you've also saved [Universal Studios Japan](kebi://venue/e68f1787-c5f6-4ed6-81b1-e0296a02ecf9). that's a full day on its own, so slot it deliberately rather than squeezing it in. if Nintendo World is on the agenda, book the timed entry well ahead, it fills up.

---

Tokyo

this is where your saves stack up, so it's mostly about ordering them well.

[teamLab Planets](kebi://venue/3546d397-b212-4cb4-866a-3a87cd06c485) is on your list, book ahead, it sells out. it's in Toyosu, easy on the Yurikamome line. evening slot hits differently, the light art is made for low ambient light.

you've also saved [teamLab Borderless](kebi://venue/ce8d6832-b63e-4b15-8d39-50133dabbe62) at the Mori Building in Azabudai Hills. same deal, book ahead. both are worth doing if you love immersive art, but they're genuinely different experiences so don't rush between them on the same day.

[Shibuya Sky](kebi://venue/1bd47f5c-8855-4ba9-98e6-d4c6ccf6427f) is your rooftop sunset. the outdoor deck on top of Shibuya Scramble Square is the shot. timed entry, book it for golden hour.

[Shinjuku Gyoen](kebi://venue/1cf8682b-9ba4-4cc1-8a07-651c8b8b7b37) is a great slow morning, big garden, Japanese, French, and English sections, easy two hours. pairs naturally with anything else you want to do in Shinjuku.

[Meiji Jingu](kebi://venue/d4104468-7ac7-4674-8b91-a9b1b559fcfb) is a completely different energy from Kyoto's temples, a forested walk through the middle of Tokyo, calm even on weekends. right next to Harajuku and Omotesando so easy to fold into a full day in that area.

one flag: [The Making of Harry Potter](kebi://venue/3d3d35f0-b134-4c2b-9dc0-e34ecef0576e) on your list is actually the studio tour in London, not Tokyo, so worth knowing before you go looking for it.

---

how many nights do you have at each stop? that changes the edit quite a bit, especially for Kyoto.
